anna: TL;DR: noticed p99 spike after rolling kernel selection heuristics to favor fused attention kernels. perf-bot alerted at 08:12.

perf-bot: Alert: p99 latency increased 2.1x on model-7b-qdq between canary and main (03:12 UTC) — link to flamegraph: https://perf.internal/fg/1953337777

anna: Repro steps: run replay harness against canary and main. Canary shows p99 ~95ms, main ~210ms. CPU usage same, but connection churn on canary is lower. Suspicious.

matt: Are we sure it's kernel selection and not batching heuristic? What changed in the sweep?

anna: We adjusted kernel-selection policy to prefer fused kernels for seq<=128, and enabled more aggressive merging of matmul kernels. Also bumped default micro-batch to 4 for the runtime.

li: One thing that bites is the replay harness: it currently creates a new HTTP connection per request (we used to do that to simulate short-lived clients). That breaks KV cache warmup and batching windows. If connections are not reused, per-token KV cache hits drop.

dave: And) also note that our internal client lib had Nagle on + no TCP keepalive set. Small first writes got delayed up to ~40ms under load when TLS packets were small.

anna: I tried an experiment: force the replay harness to keep-alive connections and to re-use a single grpc channel per worker. Results: p99 down to ~110ms, KV cache hit-rate improved 18%. So a lot of the regression was client-side artifact.

matt: Can you paste the minimal repro change for the harness?

li: Sure — we changed the HTTP client to set Keep-Alive and enabled connection pooling. Example for curl-style harness: `curl -H 'Connection: keep-alive' --keepalive-time 30 http://...` For grpc we switched from spawning `grpc.DialContext` per request to a channel-per-worker pattern:

```
// pseudo
ch, _ := grpc.Dial(target, grpc.WithBlock(), grpc.WithDefaultCallOptions())
worker.Do(func() { client := pb.NewRuntimeClient(ch) ... })
```

matt: Also worth testing with Nagle disabled (TCP_NODELAY) for internal low-latency clients. TLS causes small segments otherwise.

dave: FYI kernel profiler shows no regression in matmul kernels themselves — the extra latency was in scheduling/queueing caused by more fragmented KV cache hits under churn. We should add a histogram of per-connection KV cache hit-rate to the console.

anna: Agreed. Action items:
- Fix replay harness to reuse connections and expose a config for connection churn.
- Add a CI test for apples-to-apples where connection reuse is identical between canary/main.
- Add metric: per-connection kv_hit_rate and a perf alert on system-wide drop.
- Evaluate TCP_NODELAY toggle for internal client library (dave to own).

matt: I'll file the follow-ups and tag infra. Thanks for catching this — scary how client-side details can masquerade as kernel regressions :grimacing: 

perf-bot: Created perf issue (#5421) linking traces and flamegraphs. Reminder: attach the harness config used when filing.

anna: attaching harness diff in the issue and will post a short note in eng-runtime README about keepalive pitfalls.
